agree.reason: The frank account of the refunded campaign and the bank match would move this reader, but the pitch leaves out the $11,000 already pledged, the Thanksgiving reopening and the quarterly spending reports, all of which would have done more to win over someone who just gave elsewhere and has been let down before.

honest.reason: The numbers are accurate (85/120 is about 30% less), but 'no movies at all' for many families goes further than the facts support, and leaving out that the roof estimate could rise up to 15% hides a known risk.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 76-mile round trip and the 30% cut, but it misses that the $11,000 in written business pledges brings the public's share down to $49,000, which is the most encouraging true figure it could have given.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative fairly as a dark screen and a 38-mile drive, and it compares this campaign with the last one honestly, though it says nothing about what happens to the building if this campaign fails.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing refund promise is left as a bracketed, tentative line with no amount or date attached to it, and the possible 15% rise in the roof cost is never stated.

objections.reason: It meets the 'last time ended in refunds' objection directly, but it doesn't answer a donor with stretched finances who has just given to the ambulance fund, and it doesn't say when the cinema would reopen or how the money will be accounted for.

fit.reason: It is an appropriately short crowdfunding pitch under 350 words, but the unfilled placeholders for the cinema, bank and chair's name mean it isn't ready to publish.
